newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog sets draft paper on new fund vehicle.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog sets draft paper on new fund vehicle.

text.p: The Securities and Investment Board (SIB) said on Monday it had issued a consultative paper on its proposals to regulate a new type of British fund vehicle, open-ended investment companies (OEICs).
"In order for...OEICs to exist alongside unit trusts, certain technical amendments to the unit trust regulations need to be made," it said in a statement.
For example, the investment powers of unit trusts have to be adapted to enable them to invest in onshore OEICs.
Amendments need to be in place when onshore OEICs start next year.

The board is also reviewing its unit trust regulations in the wake of problems at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, three of whose funds were temporarily suspended pending investigation into the valuation of unlisted specualtive stocks they contained.
Any proposals for changes would be the subject of consultation in the new year, alongside any similar amendments to the OEICs regulations, it added.
